DISTRICT 9 - CGD-GL MSI/General/Miscellaneous

The Coast Guard has transitioned to a visual Maritime Safety Information Products application for the transmission of relevant information previously contained in the published Local Notice to Mariners and Coast Guard Light List. The application, which is accessible at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi, contains the most up to date maritime information overlayed on nautical charts and plotted using latitude and longitude. While the ability to print Local Notice to Mariners and Light List copies is still temporarily available, these printed products lack the positional accuracy of the electronic application and can therefore lead to relevant information being overlooked. Mariners are strongly encouraged to use the Maritime Safety Information Products application as their primary source for all information previously contained in the Local Notic

Mariners may contact L/D Nr. 3 via VHF-FM Channel 14, or at (651) 290-5062, for additional information.

Continuing until further notice, the M/V ANGELA K., is conducting dredging operations in the vicinity of Mile 702.2.  Work will be conducted from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.  The M/V ANGELA K., will monitor VHF-FM Channel 12 or 13 and requests 30-minutes advance notice of passage.  Mariners are urged to transit the area at their slowest safe speed and proceed with caution after passing arrangements have been made.

Continuing until further notice, the Dredge GOETZ will be conducting dredging operations between approximate Miles 504.0 and 502.0.  Operations will be conducted 24-hours a day, 7-days a week.  Dredge GOETZ and the attendant plant include tender boats, small boats, barges and pipeline.  Dredged material will be pumped through a pontoon pipeline, which may be crossing the channel, and is placed outside of the navigation channel.  Mariners should be on the lookout for tender boats, barges, small survey boats, and pontoon pipeline when transiting the dredge area.  Dredge GOETZ will monitor VHF-FM Channels 13, 16 and 82, and requests 45-minute advance notice of passage.  Mariners are urged to transit at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake and proceed with caution after passing arrangements have been made.
